The staff have always been friendly, helpful, and approachable.

However, I was never a fan of the previous appointment system, which required calling at 8am and repeatedly trying to get through, often only to be told that all appointments were full and to call back the next morning. This cycle frequently repeated itself and was particularly stressful when unwell. Rather than being offered the next available appointment, the system felt unfair, as someone with a new problem who happened to get through later could potentially be seen before you, despite you having already tried to make contact on earlier days. It became a “fastest finger first” approach, adding unnecessary pressure and stress for patients.

Having experienced this process personally, as well as with family members, I’m very pleased that Brooke Surgery has now introduced appointment requests via WhatsApp. I’ve used this system a couple of times and found it to be a much better experience. It does use some Ai/chatbot, but as long as you provide the requested information, the triage process works well and directs you appropriately to the needed sane day appointment.

I have previously given glowing reviews of The Brooke Surgery but over the last 24 hours had the most shocking experience which could well have been detrimental to the health of my 9 year old little boy. He started with croup like symptoms yesterday morning and I submitted an ask my GP request but his condition worsened and in the past he has suffered such severe episodes of croup that he's been unable to breathe, we therefore decided to take him to Stepping Hill Hospital fighting through rush hour traffic and when we were just a few minutes away from A&E we got a call to say they had an appointment and insisted we turn round and go to them who could treat him rather than queue in A&E for hours. I specifically asked them do they have dexamethosone to administer in case his condition worsened by the time we got there to which I was assured they did and could treat him with if needed. When we got there they made us wait until 6 other patients were seen then the paramedic who saw him said he did appear to have croup from his barky cough but that there was nothing he could do to help him as they DONT carry dexamethosone on the premises and that we need to immediately take him to A&E 🤦🏻‍♀️ When we got to A&E he was quickly triaged and they immediately administered dexamethosone then he was released 4 hours later when the cough eased slightly. The next morning he woke up with a cough a little harsh but not as harsh as the previous morning but more persistent. I used his blue inhaler as he has severe asthma but the cough only got worse - as my little boy is terrified of hospitals I put an ask my GP request through for someone to call me and say a GP couldn't see him but they'd like him to be seen by a paramedic so I explained the previous days experience & they assured me my little boy would be dealt with properly today. Now I am certain they said 11:30am but we have had a close family member diagnosed with a rare, advanced & aggressive cancer the past few weeks so my head is a little all over the place and I'd been up all night checking on my little boy so couldnt 100% say they definitely said 11:30am. We arrived at the surgery at 11:20 and there was a queue of about 3 people, while I was queueing the receptionist told the lady in front of me to use the screen to check in which I went to do but then decided to let the lady with the baby ahead of me and she had trouble getting it to accept her details - eventually she did it and I went to log in and it wouldn't let me so Dad queued behind an elderly gentleman who was speaking for a good while to the receptionist and by the time we got to speak to her she said 'you've missed your appointment so you won't now be seen' but I'll ask the clinician then 10 mins later shouted my little boys name and said the clinician would not agree to see him?! He's 9 with a complex health history which has seen him become unresponsive several times before including severe asthma and recurrent croup and they refused to see him?! I thought highly of The Brooke Surgery previously but when your conduct and lack of duty of care to a 9 year old is such that you refuse to see him when he's stood in your Surgery that is not only unacceptable it's dangerous! As was the previous days experience! I called to report the incident to the surgery straight after and asked to speak to the practice manager and not one person called. I called PALS who after hearing our experience said they did have a duty of care to my little boy that they failed to meet and to contact gm-complaints which I have now done. You can be as negligent as you feel you need to be to prove a point with adults but with children? There were also three separate times where I made an appointment with a doctor, only to get there, the appointment just didn't exist, and the receptionist dealing with it just could not care less, or offer any apologies, making you feel like you’re in the wrong when it's them. Doctors never seemed to have read any of the patient notes or files, and made rash judgements that left me upset after most visits. There were ableist comments from two doctors, and as a patient with a chronic illness I was often left feeling like they didn’t believe me or have any up to date knowledge of the condition. I ended up filing a complaint after a very frustrating and abelist conversation about trying to be registered as housebound (a very hard process for something so simple), in which the conversation left me upset. I’ve had a few problems being properly investigated since joining Brooke Surgery after years of seeing other doctors with no results.

Their social media updates are very useful and were much appreciated during the height of the pandemic. The Brooke Surgery is a refreshing practice that is actually moving with the times and giving their patients a better service because of it. have used the Ask my GP service several times and can recommend it wholeheartedly. I have found it a very efficient service. It's very easy to use, I am not very tech savvy and in my 60s. You start by giving brief details of your issue and whether it is an existing or new problem. Then you can describe your symptoms in detail. In this section give as much detail as you can, if you imagine a person in front of you, just describe  your problem as if they were there. Use your own words, give pain levels say on a scale of 1 to 10. It's confidential and secure, look for the little lock symbol at the top. You can choose  how you would like to be answered, email, phonecall, video, or face to face appointment. If you need a prescription that is sent to  the Well pharmacy across the road. This is the weak link. The pharmacy is slap bang in the middle of two busy surgeries and I think they are struggling  to cope. On several occasions  they have only prepared  my prescription when I have enquired about it, despite putting in my repeat prescription at the Surgery for approval, a week in advance.  They tell you that the surgery has only just sent it to them. Overall though it's brilliant and I will continue to use it for as long as it is available. If you are not able to use it yourself your carer can use it for you and this question is asked.
